title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer
description:
If you've built something before, start here The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.
 What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.
 
 About Scalera Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.
 
 What you'll do You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.
 Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

 Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

 Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

 Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

 Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

 Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

 
 What success looks like after 3 months There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

 You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

 You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

 At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

 You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

 
 You'll probably thrive here if You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

 You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both

 You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data

 You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec

 You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is

 You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title

 Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going

 You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls

 You make things simpler over time, not more clever

 You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement

 
 You probably won't enjoy it if You just want to code and go home

 You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit

 Ambiguity and chaos bother you

 You want a well-defined backlog handed to you

 Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount

 
 Our stack Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.
 
 How we hire Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

 Technical deep-dive call : walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.

 Meet Scalera Day : come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.

 Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

 
 Working at Scalera Zürich HQ, four days in the office, Fridays remote

 Occasional customer visits across Switzerland, Austria and Germany

 Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

 Competitive salary and equity

 
 Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

title: Software Engineer, Web Crawling
description:
Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z.
  
 Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you.
  
 As a Web Crawler engineer, you'd be responsible for crawling the entire web. Basically build Google-scale crawling!
 
 Who You Are You have extensive experience building and scaling web crawlers, or would be excited to ramp up very quickly

 You have experience with some high performance language (C++, Rust, etc.)

 You are familiar with TypeScript, Playwright, modern web design, CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol)

 You’re comfortable optimizing a system to an exceptional degree

 You care about the problem of finding high quality knowledge and recognize how important this is for the world

 
 What You Could Do Build a distributed crawler that can handle 100M+ pages per day

 Optimize crawl politeness and rate limiting across thousands of domains

 Design systems to detect and handle dynamic content, JavaScript rendering, and anti-bot measures

 Create intelligent crawl scheduling and prioritization algorithms for maximum coverage efficiency

 
 Logistics Location: This is an in-person opportunity in San Francisco.

 Visas: We're happy to sponsor international candidates (e.g., STEM OPT, OPT, H1B, O1, E3). While we cannot guarantee your visa, we have historically been successful in sponsoring candidates from all over the world. If you receive an offer, our team will work hard to get you a visa.

 Benefits: We offer premium healthcare benefits (medical, dental, vision), fertility benefits, 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents, and a monthly wellness stipend to all of our employees.

 Exa is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related conditions, criminal histories consistent with applicable law, or any other basis protected by applicable law.
